hooks.text: The Sun and Moon look identical in our sky.
The Sun is 400 times wider than the Moon.
The Sun is massive, yet looks Moon-sized.

title: The 400X Cosmic Match Behind Total Eclipses
description: The Sun is 400 times wider than the Moon and 400 times farther away, creating a near-perfect size match in Earth's sky.

beats.text: The Sun and Moon look identical in our sky.
beats.visual: photograph of the Sun and Moon matching size during a total solar eclipse

beats.text: Most people assume they are naturally similar in size.
beats.visual: diagram of Earth Moon and Sun orbit alignment
queries: solar eclipse diagram Earth Moon Sun

beats.text: But the Sun is roughly 400 times wider than the Moon.
beats.visual: scale comparison graphic of the Sun and Moon sizes

beats.text: It is also 400 times farther away from Earth.
beats.visual: diagram showing distance from Earth to Moon and Sun
queries: solar eclipse geometry diagram umbra penumbra

beats.text: That matching ratio makes both objects span half a degree.
beats.visual: illustration of angular size calculation in sky

beats.text: During totality, the Moon covers the Sun's disk completely.
beats.visual: photograph of solar corona visible during totality
queries: Solar corona total solar eclipse photograph

beats.text: Artemis astronauts will even watch a 57-minute eclipse in space.
beats.visual: illustration of NASA Orion spacecraft performing Artemis II lunar flyby
queries: Artemis II Orion lunar flyby illustration
Orion spacecraft Artemis II Moon concept

beats.text: That is why both distant worlds look identical in our sky.
